Adele Fornarino - Submeta - Overhook Clo.overview: A compact Submeta course (about an hour) from Adele Fornarino, an ADCC-level competitor, on building a closed guard game around the overhook. It is organised as a learning path: key concepts first (how the overhook works, push and pull, distance, how to get it from closed guard), then the attacks (triangle, armbar, belly-down armbar, keeping pressure in the armbar), the sweeps you transition to when they defend (scissor, elevation, flower), troubleshooting (a sweep, the Mir lock, what to do when they keep their arms tight) and a summary.
Adele Fornarino - Submeta - Overhook Clo.for: Closed guard players in no-gi who struggle to attack opponents with good posture.
key: Triangle and armbar from the overhook
Mir lock when they hide their arms

Adele Fornarino - Submeta - Top Pins to.overview: A short Submeta course (about 45 minutes) on moving from top pins to the back. It starts with the ideas behind creating back exposure and maintaining the 'harness' (an over-under chest grip) with a solo drill, then shows the basic chair-sit transition. After that it covers transitions from side control, knee ride and mount, the gift wrap (trapping an arm across the neck) leading to an armbar or kimura, troubleshooting when they don't turn or keep their arms tight, and a summary.
Adele Fornarino - Submeta - Top Pins to.for: Top players who pin well but don't get to the back.
key: Back takes from side control, knee ride and mount
Gift wrap to armbar or kimura

Andrew Tackett - Inside & Outside NoGi P.overview: Three short lessons from Andrew Tackett (one of the Tackett brothers of Pedigo Submission Fighting) on the hand positions that drive no-gi passing: inside hand positioning, outside hand positioning, and inside versus outside ankle control. The third file appears to be incomplete (it has no length information and may not play properly).
Andrew Tackett - Inside & Outside NoGi P.for: No-gi passers who want to understand where their hands should be.

files.03 Inside And Outside Ankle Control .mp4: Inside versus outside ankle control. This file looks incomplete and may not play.

AOJ Cole Abate K Guard Masterclass.overview: Cole Abate's K guard masterclass from Art of Jiu Jitsu (the Mendes brothers' academy), about 4.5 hours. After the fundamentals of the K guard (an inverted, leg-entangling open guard), it covers off-balancing standing and kneeling opponents, then how to enter the K guard against specific passes: the knee slide (with Gui Mendes), the toreando, the long step and the stack pass. It finishes with sweeps, submissions and a long private-lesson style session.
AOJ Cole Abate K Guard Masterclass.for: Gi open guard players who want to add the K guard, especially against modern passers.
key: Entering the K guard against knee slide, toreando, long step and stack passes

files.06.Entering the K Guard Versus Knee Slid: Using the K guard against the knee slide, with Gui Mendes.
files.12.Private Lesson with Mick And Rai.mp4: A private-lesson style session with Mick and Rai.

AOKI.overview: Japanese DVD rips of Shinya Aoki instructionals, in Japanese. SPD-3518 is 'Super Grappling Techniques' (about 1h 45m main feature) and SPD-3616 is 'Super Grappling Techniques Vol 2' (about 1h 40m main feature, plus a 26-minute extra, reportedly a 2007 Shooto fight against Akira Kikuchi). SPD-3826 (about 1h 50m main feature) is likely a later Aoki DVD; its title couldn't be confirmed. Aoki's style is creative submission grappling for gi, no-gi and MMA: flexible guard work, leg locks, armlocks and attacks on the neck such as guillotines from top. Reviews describe the discs as mostly demonstration.
AOKI.for: Fans of Aoki's creative submission style; you'll need to follow by watching, as it isn't in English.
key: Neck attacks and guillotines from top
sources: Budovideos listings for SPD-3518 and SPD-3616 (Super Grappling Techniques Vol 1 and 2).

B Mac/The Lockdown.overview: A single 70-minute lesson from Brandon 'B-Mac' McCaghren on the lockdown half guard: securing the lockdown, using the whip-up to break the opponent's posture, and the sweeps and back takes that follow.
B Mac/The Lockdown.for: Half guard players who want the 10th Planet lockdown.
sources: Based on the title and B-Mac's published lockdown material.

Back In Control.overview: Mason Fowler's back course (Digitsu, about 2 hours) covering both sides of back control: taking the back, basic back escapes, escapes when the attacker has only one hook in (including escaping to 50/50 and to the knees with an underhook) and how the attacker counters them, dealing with a standing opponent, and attacks from the back.
Back In Control.for: Anyone who wants to take and keep the back, and know the escapes they'll face.
key: Keeping the back on a standing opponent

files.01 Taking the Back.mp4: Back takes, including an advanced back take and the hug-body-and-pull-knee-through take.
files.02 Basic Back Escapes.mp4: The basic escapes and how to counter them as the attacker.
files.03 One Hook Escapes.mp4: Escapes when only one hook is in: to 50/50, to the knees with an underhook, the classic escape, and countering them.
files.04 Standing Opponent.mp4: Keeping back control when the opponent stands up.

Barry Robinson - A Million Styles - Catc.overview: A boxing instructional, not BJJ. Barry Robinson's 'A Million Styles' series teaches boxing technique; this volume focuses on catching punches (parrying and blocking with the gloves) and immediately firing back with counters.
Barry Robinson - A Million Styles - Catc.for: Striking practice; not relevant to jiu-jitsu.
sources: Based on the series title; Barry Robinson's 'A Million Styles' boxing series is sold by Dynamic Striking / BJJ Fanatics.

Basic Grip Breaking- Travis Stevens.overview: Six very short lessons (about 12 minutes in total) from Olympic judo silver medallist Travis Stevens on breaking common gi grips from standing: the cross collar grip, a grip on the end of your sleeve, the cat's paw sleeve grip, the double collar grip (two variations) and a high grip on your shoulder.
Basic Grip Breaking- Travis Stevens.for: Gi players who get controlled in grip fights when standing.
key: Dealing with a high shoulder grip
